indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.2.3: Know that substances can exist in different physical state (solid, liquid, Gas). Many substances can be changed from one state to another by heating or cooling
indicator.objective: Explain how substances change state between solid, liquid and gas

skills.description: Explain that substances can change state when heated or cooled
Give examples of substances changing state
Explain simply why a substance changes state
Demonstrate or describe an observation of a substance changing state

misconceptions: Melting and freezing are the same thing.
Steam is not water; it is smoke.
When water boils, it disappears completely.
Ice is a different substance from water.
Condensation is when water turns into ice.

questions.stem: What happens to ice when it is left in the sun?
questions.explanation: Heating ice causes it to melt and change from a solid to a liquid (water).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think ice stays solid.

questions.stem: What happens to water when you put it in a freezer?
questions.explanation: Cooling water causes it to freeze and change from a liquid to a solid (ice).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the freezer boils the water.

questions.stem: What do we call water when it is in the form of a gas?
hints: It comes from a boiling kettle.
questions.explanation: Water in its gaseous state is called steam or water vapour.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think steam is smoke.

questions.stem: Which of these is a solid form of water?
questions.explanation: Ice is the solid form of water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think rain is solid.

questions.stem: What causes water to turn into steam?
hints: You put it on a fire.
questions.explanation: Heating water to its boiling point causes it to turn into steam (a gas).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think adding cold causes steam.

questions.stem: When water vapour (steam) hits a cold window, it turns into liquid water droplets. What is this change called?
hints: You see drops on the glass.
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change of state from a gas to a liquid.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse it with melting.

questions.stem: Butter changes from solid to liquid when you put it in a hot pan. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: The change from a solid to a liquid is called melting.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think it is boiling.

questions.stem: Why does a puddle of water dry up on a hot day?
options: The water evaporates into the air
The water turns into a solid
The water hides in the ground
hints: It goes into the air as a gas.
questions.explanation: The heat from the sun causes the liquid water to evaporate into water vapour (a gas) in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the water just vanishes.

questions.stem: Ice is a solid. Water is a liquid. What is the process of ice turning into water?
hints: It happens when it gets warm.
questions.explanation: Ice melts into water when it gains heat.

questions.stem: Name one example of a gas changing into a liquid.
answer: steam turning to water on a cold glass
questions.explanation: Steam condensing on a cold surface is a gas-to-liquid change.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know the word condensation.

questions.stem: What do we call the process when a liquid turns into a solid?
questions.explanation: The process of a liquid turning into a solid is called freezing.

questions.stem: Why do we put water in the fridge to make it cold?
options: The fridge removes heat from the water
The fridge adds cold to the water
The fridge makes the water evaporate
questions.explanation: The fridge removes heat from the water, lowering its temperature.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the fridge adds 'cold' to the water.

questions.stem: Which of these changes happens when a gas is cooled?
options: It turns into a solid directly (always)
questions.explanation: Cooling a gas causes it to condense into a liquid.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cooling a gas always makes a solid.

questions.stem: Why does a water bottle left in the sun become warm?
options: It gains heat from the sun
It loses heat to the sun
hints: The sun is a source of heat.
Heat moves from hot to cold.
questions.explanation: The sun transfers heat to the water bottle, raising its temperature.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the bottle creates heat.

questions.stem: A substance changes from a solid to a liquid and then to a gas. What must happen for these changes to occur?
options: It must stay in the dark
questions.explanation: Both melting and boiling require the substance to gain heat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cooling causes these changes.

questions.stem: Explain what happens to the water particles when ice melts.

criteria.description: States that the ice gains heat
States that the solid ice turns into liquid water

questions.explanation: When ice melts, it gains heat, causing the solid ice to change into liquid water.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how you can change a piece of ice into water.

criteria.description: Places the ice in a warm area or holds it
Observes and explains that the solid ice melts into liquid water due to heat

hints: What happens if you hold ice in your hand?
questions.explanation: The heat from the hand or room causes the ice to melt into water.

questions.stem: Describe an experiment you can do at home to see water change from liquid to gas.

criteria.description: States boiling water in a kettle or pot

hints: What happens when you boil water?
What comes out of the kettle?
questions.explanation: Boiling water produces steam, which is water changing from a liquid to a gas.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is TRUE?
options: Water can exist as a solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam)
Water only exists as a liquid
Ice is a different substance from water
hints: Can you freeze water? Can you boil it?
questions.explanation: Water is the same substance in all three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think ice and steam are different substances.

questions.stem: Explain why a glass of cold water gets wet on the outside on a hot day.

criteria.description: States that water vapour in the air cools when it touches the cold glass
States that the vapour condenses into liquid water droplets

hints: Is the glass colder than the air?
What happens to gas when it cools?
questions.explanation: The cold glass cools the water vapour in the air, causing it to condense into liquid water droplets on the outside of the glass.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher the difference between melting and freezing.

criteria.description: States melting is solid to liquid
States freezing is liquid to solid

questions.explanation: Melting is changing from solid to liquid. Freezing is changing from liquid to solid.
